REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - FEBRUARY 14, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.
1.
Call to Order
2.
Invocation
The California Court of Appeal has concluded that sectarian prayer as part of the City Council meetings is not permitted under the Constitution.
Invocation - Revised

Pledge of Allegiance - Revised
4.

5.
Presentations/Appointments
5A.
Presentations
Presentations
6.
Public Comments and Suggestions
This section is reserved for comments related to Consent Calendar Items and items not listed on the Agenda but within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council/Successor Agency. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the City Council/Successor Agency, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.
7A.
Approval of Minutes
Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
January 24, 2019 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Minutes
7B.
Approval of Registers of Demands
7B.1.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated February 14, 2019 (COUNCIL).
City Register
7B.2.
Approval of the Register of Demands for the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency dated February 14, 2019 (SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
Agency Register
(Pursuant to City Council approval Item 7C was removed from Consent and considered separately)
7C.
Adoption of Ordinance
Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of January 24, 2019:
Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1024, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING CHAPTER 22.42, WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS, OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE, ADDING A DEFINITION FOR A SMALL WIRELESS FACILITY AND CLARIFYING REQUIREMENTS AND REGULATIONS FOR SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES, HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-3 (COUNCIL).*
*Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.
Adoption of Ordinance
8.
Public Hearings
8A.
Recommendation by the Cerritos Planning Commission, on a vote of 4-0-1, with one Commissioner abstaining, to approve the following:
Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING TITLE 9 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING CHAPTER 9.83, ESTABLISHING REGULATIONS FOR SIDEWALK VENDORS IN THE CITY OF CERRITOS, AND AMENDING CHAPTER 9.48 OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE IN RESPONSE TO CALIFORNIA SENATE BILL 946 (2018), HEREIN REFERENCED AS DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-2 (COUNCIL).*
*Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this project is categorically exempt from CEQA Review.
Agenda Report
8B.
Review and consideration of a request for authorization for the City of Cerritos (landlord) to lease City-owned property located at 17423 Studebaker Road, Cerritos, California, 90703, to AutoNation (tenant), pursuant to terms of a Letter of Intent (LOI), for the storage of new automobiles to be made available for sale at the Cerritos Auto Square. The subject property is zoned Development Area Fifteen (ADP-15), with an overlay zoning designation of Area Development Plan 5.1 (ADP-5.1) Cerritos Auto Square Overlay Zone, measures approximately ±1.19 acres, and is currently vacant and undeveloped (APN 7034-016-910) (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9.
New and Old Business
(Pursuant to City Council approval Item 9A. was heard out of order)
9A.
Review and consideration of an informational report on the Public Safety equipment donation from the Picerne Family Foundation, a 501(c)(3) organization, and the City's acquisition of new Public Safety equipment for use by the Cerritos Sheriff's Station deputies (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9B.
Review and consideration of a request for authorization for the City of Cerritos to acquire two (2) very-low income affordable senior housing units located within the Emerald Villas affordable senior housing community, for the purpose of making said units available for sale to qualified senior residents, in accordance with previously recorded covenants, applicable re-sale guidelines and California State Housing Law. The subject properties are located at 19427 Topaz Court, Unit G, and 19423 Sapphire Court, Unit N, Cerritos, California, 90703 (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9C.
Review and consideration of an informational report on Senate Bill 998 (Dodd, D-Napa), the Water Shutoff Protection Act, and its potential impact on the City of Cerritos (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
9D.
Review and consideration of award of Bid No. 1357-19, a contract for Gridley Park and Reservoir Hill Park improvements, Project Nos. 19102 and 19104 (COUNCIL).
Agenda Report
10.
Legislative Items
10A.
Report on pending legislation.
10B.
Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
11.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.
Closed Session
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
FEBRUARY 14, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Jeff Ludington, Generations Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Steelers Junior Future League
  Player Jeremiah Dunklin and Noah Freeman, and Cerritos Hornets Youth
  Football Player Austin Miller.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Proclamations were made as follows:

  Cerritos Steelers Junior Future League (6 and Under Super Bowl Champions).

  Cerritos Hornets Youth Football (7 and Under Western Conference Champions).

  Cerritos Steelers Junior Clinic (8 and Under Super Bowl Champions).

  Cerritos Steelers Clinic (10 and Under Commissioners Cup Winner).

  Cerritos Steelers Pee Wee (13 and Under Commissioners Cup Winner).

  Picerne Family Foundation (In recognition of their public safety equipment
  donation to the Cerritos Sheriff’s Station and donation to the Cerritos Center for
  the Performing Arts).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Scott Smith, Executive Director, Cerritos Regional Chamber of Commerce,
  spoke on behalf of Gigi Meese, 3D Theatricals, regarding the new Broadway
  series production at the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Lorna Brandes spoke regarding concerns with multiple vehicle accidents in front
  of her property and submitted written correspondence for the record.

  Case Van der Linden spoke regarding the condition of City streets.

7C.  Adoption of Ordinance

  Ordinance introduced at the regular meeting of January 24, 2019:

  Waive full reading of and adopt Ordinance No. 1024, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY  OF  CERRITOS  AMENDING  CHAPTER  22.42, WIRELESS
  TELECOMMUNICATIONS, OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE, ADDING A
  DEFINITION FOR A SMALL WIRELESS FACILITY AND CLARIFYING REQUIREMENTS
  AND REGULATIONS FOR SMALL WIRELESS FACILITIES, HEREIN REFERENCED AS
  DEVELOPMENT CODE AMENDMENT 2019-3 (COUNCIL).*

  This item was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and

  equipment donation from the Picerne Family Foundation, a 501(c)(3)

  by the Cerritos Sheriff's Station deputies (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager. A PowerPoint

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  the Picerne Family Foundation’s generous contribution to public safety and
  acknowledge those willing to don the armor in protection of others (COUNCIL).

  to acquire two (2) very-low income affordable senior housing units located

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute, acknowledge, and
